To watch or tend someone else's child for a period of time, often for money.
d.x: My daughter is babysitting for the Morgans at number ten, who are going out on a date night.

d.d: To watch or tend a thing or process without normally intervening in it, e.g. as a precaution should an emergency happen.
d.x: The reaction takes several hours, so we leave a graduate student to babysit it.

d.d: To watch or attend anything or anyone more closely than ought to be needed; to have to help or coax too much.
d.x: He left me to babysit the new guy while he got some work done.

d.d: A person who cares for one or more babies or children for a short period of time in place of their legal guardians.
d.x: My neighbor is sometimes a babysitter for other mothers’ children.
